chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Ja'far ibn Muhammad that Ali (peace be upon him) said:

The talbiyah of the mute person, his tashahhud, and his recitation of the Quran in prayer is the movement of his tongue and his pointing with his finger. And there is no harm if a person says the talbiyah while he is not in a state of ritual purity, and in every state, that was narrated.

key_terms.الْأَخْرَسِ: The mute person (one who cannot speak)
key_terms.تَلْبِيَةُ: Talbiyah (the declaration 'Here I am, O God' said during Hajj or prayer)

ai.seo_question: How does a mute person perform the talbiyah and Quran recitation during prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq clarifies the fiqh of the mute person, establishing that internal intention coupled with physical gestures (talking with the tongue, pointing with the finger) suffices for the essential pillars of prayer, including the Talbiyah and Quran recitation. It further highlights the distinct legal status of the Talbiyah as a declaration of intent rather than a strict pillar of prayer, thereby allowing it to be recited even in a state of minor impurity (hadath), a nuance valued in Shia jurisprudence for understanding the flexibility of worship.
